findings.description: The 'data' bucket is explicitly marked as public in a comment and has no ACL restriction, exposing any stored objects to the entire internet. For a bucket holding customer data this is a significant data exposure risk.
The 'data' bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so objects stored at rest are unencrypted, exposing customer data if the underlying storage is accessed.
The bucket does not have access logging configured, so there is no audit trail of access to customer data, hampering security monitoring and incident response.
The bucket does not have versioning enabled, so accidental deletion or overwrite of customer data cannot be recovered, and tampering cannot be detected.
This object contains customer-master.xlsx, a sensitive customer data file, and is stored in an unencrypted bucket with no default encryption or object-level encryption configured.
The 'financials' bucket has no server-side encryption, leaving financial data unencrypted at rest.
The financials bucket has no access logging enabled, so there is no audit trail for access to sensitive financial data.
The financials bucket does not have versioning enabled, so accidental modification or deletion of financial data cannot be rolled back.
The 'operations' bucket has no server-side encryption, leaving operational data unencrypted at rest.
The operations bucket does not have access logging enabled, leaving no audit trail for access to operational data.
The 'data_science' bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so data at rest is unencrypted.
